in the basic texts. In the case of the SV, the HB and the VN, the first three figures
indicate the page number, and the last two indicate the line number (for example,
SV16026=SV 160,26; HB02314=HB 23,14; VN06110=VN 61,10). In the case of the
PV and the NB, the second figure indicates the chapter number and the last three
figures indicate the karika or sutra number (for example, PV02232=PV, the
Pramanasiddhi-chapter v.232; NB03015=NB, the Pararthanumana-chapter sutra 15.
In the case of the SP, the last two figures indicate the karika number (for example,
SP00015=SP, v.15).

children.translated_text: 3. In this database, sentences are artificially divided into word-units, although they involve a phonetic fusion or union in the basic texts. Further, compound words are divided into their shortest constitutive elements (we use a hyphen to indicate that hyphenated elements originally form a compound word) with the following exceptions:

children.text:
3.1. The prefixes a-, dur-, nih- remain undivided, irrespective of attachment to
words or compound words.
children.translated_text: 3.1. The prefixes a-, dur-, niḥ- remain undivided, irrespective of attachment to words or compound words.

children.text:
3.2. Suffixes making an adverb, for example -vat, -vasa, are divided. But suffixes
making a possessive adjective, for example -vat, -mat, remain undivided, and terms
such as a numeral+ -dha/-vidha/-prakara remain also undivided.
children.translated_text: 3.2. Suffixes making an adverb, for example -vat, -vaśa, are divided. But suffixes making a possessive adjective, for example -vat, -mat, remain undivided, and terms such as a numeral + -dhā/-vidhā/-prakāra remain also undivided.

children.text:
3.3. Compound words with the suffixes -ta/-tva or -bhava/-bhuta fundamentally
remain undivided. For example: karyakaranabhava/-bhuta/-ta.
children.translated_text: 3.3. Compound words with the suffixes -tā/-tva or -bhāva/-bhūta fundamentally remain undivided. For example: <s>kāryakāraṇabhāva</s>/-bhūta/-tā.

children.text:
3.4. Compound words with evam-, tat-, tatha-, para-, yatha-, su-, sva- in the
wordhead fundamentally remain undivided. For example: evamjatiya, tadutpatti,
tathakrta, paratantra, yathartha, yathasvam, sujnanatva, svabhava.
children.translated_text: 3.4. Compound words with evam-, tat-, tathā-, para-, yathā-, su-, sva- in the word-head fundamentally remain undivided. For example: <s>evaṃjātīya</s>, <s>tadutpatti</s>, <s>tathākṛta</s>, <s>paratantra</s>, <s>yathārtha</s>, <s>yathāsvam</s>, <s>sujñānatva</s>, <s>svabhāva</s>.

children.text:
3.5. Some compound words which are regarded as terminology remain also
undivided. For example: agnihotra, ayogavyavaccheda, arthapatti, padartha,
paramartha, prasajyapratisedha, viruddhavyabhicarin, samanantarapratyaya,
samtanaparinama, samanyalaksana, svabhavapratibandha.
children.translated_text: 3.5. Some compound words which are regarded as terminology remain also undivided. For example: <s>agnihotra</s>, <s>ayogavyavaccheda</s>, <s>arthāpatti</s>, <s>padārtha</s>, <s>paramārtha</s>, <s>prasajyapratiṣedha</s>, <s>viruddhavyabhicārin</s>, <s>samanantarapratyaya</s>, <s>saṃtānapariṇāma</s>, <s>sāmānyalakṣaṇa</s>, <s>svabhāvapratibandha</s>.

children.text:
4. Those terms whose wordhead is subject to the Sandhi rules (for example, -d
dhetu-) are cited in their original form (for example, -d *hetu-) for the sake of
using this database to make an KWIC index.
children.translated_text: 4. Those terms whose word-head is subject to the <s>sandhi</s> rules (for example, -d dhetu-) are cited in their original form (for example, -d *hetu-) for the sake of using this database to make a KWIC index.

01001 samyag-jñāna-pūrvikā sarva-puruṣa-artha-siddhir iti tad vyutpādyate.
01002 dvividhaṃ samyag-jñānam.
01003 pratyakṣam anumānaṃ ca iti.
01004 tatra pratyakṣaṃ kalpanā apoḍham abhrāntam.
01005 abhilāpa-saṃsarga-yogya-pratibhāsā pratītiḥ kalpanā.
01006 tayā rahitaṃ timira-āśubhramaṇa-nauyāna-saṃkṣobha-ādy-anāhita-vibhramaṃ jñānaṃ pratyakṣam.
01007 tat caturvidham.
01008 indriya-jñānam.
01009 sva-viṣaya-anantara-viṣaya-sahakāriṇā indriya-jñānena samanantarapratyayena janitaṃ tan manovijñānam.
01010 sarva-citta-caittānām ātma-saṃvedanam.
01011 bhūta-artha-bhāvanā-prakarṣa-paryantajaṃ yogijñānaṃ ca iti.
01012 tasya viṣayaḥ svalakṣaṇam.
01013 yasya arthasya saṃnidhāna-asaṃnidhānābhyāṃ jñāna-pratibhāsa-bhedas tat svalakṣaṇam.
01014 tad eva paramārthasat.
01015 arthakriyāsāmarthya-lakṣaṇatvād vastunaḥ.
01016 anyat sāmānyalakṣaṇam.
01017 so anumānasya viṣayaḥ.
01018 tad eva ca pratyakṣaṃ jñānaṃ pramāṇa-phalam.
01019 artha-pratīti-rūpatvāt.
01020 artha-sārūpyam asya pramāṇam.
01021 tad-vaśād artha-pratīti-siddher iti.
02001 anumānaṃ dvividhā.
02002 svārthaṃ parārthaṃ ca.
02003 tatra svārthaṃ trirūpāl liṅgād yad anumeye jñānaṃ tad anumānam.
02004 pramāṇa-phala-vyavasthā atra api pratyakṣa-vat.
02005 trairūpyaṃ punar liṅgasya anumeye sattvam eva, sapakṣa eva sattvam, asapakṣe ca asattvam eva niścitam.
02006 anumeyo atra jijñāṣita-viśeṣo dharmī.
02007 sādhya-dharma-sāmānyena samāno arthaḥ sapakṣaḥ.
02008 na sapakṣo asapakṣaḥ.
02009 tato anyas tad-viruddhas tad-abhāvaś ca iti.
02010 trirūpāṇi ca trīṇy eva liṅgāni.
02011 anupalabdhiḥ svabhāvaḥ kāryaṃ ca iti.
02012 tatra anupalabdhir yathā, na pradeśa-viśeṣe kvacid ghaṭaḥ, upalabdhi-lakṣaṇa-prāptasya anupalabdher iti
02013 upalabdhi-lakṣaṇa-prāptir upalambha-pratyaya-antara-sākalyaṃ svabhāva-viśeṣaś ca.
02014 yaḥ svabhāvaḥ satsv anyeṣu upalambha-pratyayeṣu san pratyakṣa eva bhavati sa svabhāva-viśeṣaḥ.
02015 svabhāvaḥ sva-sattā-mātra-bhāvini sādhya-dharme hetuḥ.
02016 yathā vṛkṣo ayaṃ śiṃśapātvād iti.
02017 kāryaṃ yathā vahnir atra dhūmād iti.
02018 atra dvau vastu-sādhanau. ekaḥ pratiṣedha-hetuḥ
02019 svabhāvapratibandhe hi saty artho arthaṃ gamayet.
02020 tad-apratibaddhasya tad-avyabhicāra-niyama-abhāvāt.
02021 sa ca pratibandhaḥ sādhye arthe liṅgasya.
02022 vastutas tādātmyāt tadutpatteś ca.
02023 atad-svabhāvasya atadutpatteś ca tatra apratibaddha-svabhāvatvāt.
02024 te ca tādātmya-tadupattī svabhāva-kāryayor eva iti tābhyām eva vastu-siddhiḥ.
02025 pratiṣedha-siddhir api yathoktāyā eva anupalabdheḥ.
02026 sati vastuni tasyā asambhavāt.
02027 anyathā ca anupalabdhi-lakṣaṇa-prāpteṣu deśa-kāla-svabhāva-viprakṛṣṭeṣv artheṣv ātma-pratyakṣa-nivṛtter abhāva-niścaya-abhāvāt.
02028 amūḍha-smṛti-saṃskārasya atītasya vartamānasya ca pratipattṛ-pratyakṣasya nivṛttir abhāva-vyavahāra-pravartanī.
02029 tasyā eva abhāva-niścayāt.
02030 sā ca prayoga-bhedād ekadaśa-prakārā.
02031 svabhāva-anupalabdhir yathā, na atra dhūma upalabdhi-lakṣaṇa-prāptasya anupalabdhir iti.
02032 kārya-anupalabdhir yathā, na iha apratibaddha-sāmarthyāni dhūma-kāraṇāni santi dhūma-abhāvād iti.
02033 vyāpaka-anupalabdhir yathā, na atra śiṃśapā, vṛkṣa-abhāvād iti.
02034 svabhāva-viruddha-upalabdhir yathā, na atra śīta-sparśo vahner iti.
02035 viruddha-kārya-upalabdhir yathā, na atra śīta-sparśo dhūmād iti.
02036 viruddha-vyāpta-upalabdhir yathā, na dhūma-bhāvī bhūtasya api bhāvasya vināśaḥ, hetv-antara-apekṣaṇād iti.
02037 kārya-viruddha-upalabdhir yathā, na iha apratibaddha-sāmarthyāni śīta-kāraṇāni santi, vahner iti.
02038 vyāpaka-viruddha-upalabdhir yathā, na atra tuṣāra-sparśo vahner iti.
02039 kāraṇa-anupalabdhir yathā, na atra dhūmo vahny-abhāvād iti.
02040 kāraṇa-viruddha-upalabdhir yathā, na asya roma-harṣa-ādi-viśeṣāḥ, saṃnihita-dahana-viśeṣatvād iti.
02041 kāraṇa-viruddha-kārya-upalabdhir yathā, na roma-harṣa-ādi-viśeṣa-yukta-puruṣavān ayaṃ pradeśaḥ, dhūmād iti.
02042 ime sarve kārya-anupalabdhy-ādayo daśa-anupalabdhi-prayogāḥ svabhāva-anupalabdhau saṃgraham upayānti.
02043 pāraṃparyeṇa arthāntara-vidhi-pratiṣedhāyāṃ prayoga-bhede api.
02044 prayoga-darśana-abhyāsāt svayam apy evaṃ vyavaccheda-pratītir bhavati iti svārthe apy anumāne asyāḥ prayoga-nirdeśaḥ.
02045 sarvatra ca asyām abhāva-vyavahāra-sādhanyām anupalabdhau yeṣāṃ svabhāva-viruddha-ādīnām upalabdhyā kāraṇa-ādīnām anupalabdhyā ca pratiṣedha uktas teṣām upalabdhi-lakṣaṇa-prāptānām.
02045 eva upalabdhir anupalabdhiś ca veditavyā.
02046 anyeṣāṃ virodha-kāryakāraṇabhāva-siddheḥ.
02047 pramāṇa-nivṛttav apy artha-abhāva-asiddher iti.
03001 trirūpa-liṅga-ākhyānaṃ parārtham anumānam.
03002 kāraṇe kārya-upacārāt.
03003 tad dvividham.
03004 prayoga-bhedāt.
03005 sādharmya-vaidharmya-vacana iti.
03006 na anayor arthataḥ kaścid bhedaḥ.
03007 anyatra prayoga-bhedāt.
03008 tatra sādharmyavat prayogaḥ: yad upalabdhi-lakṣaṇa-prāptaṃ sann na upalabhyate so asad-vyavahāra-viṣayaḥ siddhaḥ, yathā anyaḥ kaścid dṛṣṭaḥ śaśa-viṣāṇa-ādiḥ. na upalabhyate ca kaścit pradeśa-viśeṣa upalabdhi-lakṣaṇa-prāpto ghaṭa ity anupalabdhi-prayogaḥ.
03009 tathā svabhāvahetoḥ prayogaḥ: yat sat tat sarvam anityam, yathā ghaṭa-ādir iti śuddhasya svabhāvahetoḥ prayogaḥ.
03010 yad utpattimat tad anityam iti svabhāvabhūta-dharma-bhedena svabhāvasya prayogaḥ.
03011 yat kṛtakaṃ tad anityam ity upādhi-bhedena.
03012 apekṣita-para-vyāpāro hi bhāvaḥ svabhāva-niṣpattau kṛtaka iti.
03013 evaṃ pratyaya-bhedabheditva-ādayo api draṣṭavyāḥ.
03014 sann utpattimān kṛtako vā śabda iti pakṣa-dharma-upadarśanam.
03015 sarva ete sādhana-dharmā yathāsvaṃ pramāṇaiḥ. siddha-sādhana-dharma-mātra-anubandha eva sādhya-dharmo avagantavyāḥ.
03016 tasya eva tat.
03017 svabhāvasya ca hetutvāt.
03018 vastutas tayos tādātmyam.
03019 tan-niṣpattāv aniṣpannasya tat-svabhāvatva-abhāvāt.
03020 vyabhicāra-sambhavāc ca.
03021 kāryahetoḥ prayogaḥ: yatra dhūmas tatra agniḥ, yathā mahānasa-ādau. asti ca iha dhūma iti.
03022 iha api siddha eva kāryakāraṇabhāve kāraṇe sādhye kāryahetur vaktavyaḥ.
03023 vaidharmyavataḥ prayogaḥ: yat sad upalabdhi-lakṣaṇa-prāptaṃ tad upalabhyata eva, yathā nīla-ādi-viśeṣaḥ. na ca evam iha upalabdhi-lakṣaṇa-prāptasya sata upalabdhir ghaṭasya ity anupalabdhi-prayogaḥ.
03024 asaty anityatve na asty eva sattvam utpattimattvaṃ kṛtakatvaṃ vā. saṃś ca śabda utpattimān kṛtako vā iti svabhāvahetoḥ prayogaḥ.
03025 asaty agnau na bhavaty eva dhūmaḥ. atra ca asti dhūma iti kāryahetoḥ prayogaḥ.
03026 sādharmyeṇa api hi prayoge arthād vaidharmya-gatir iti.
03027 asati tasmin sādhyena hetor anvaya-abhāvāt.
03028 tathā vaidharmyeṇa apy anvaya-gatiḥ.
03029 asati tasmin sādhya-abhāve hetv-abhāvasya asiddheḥ.
03030 na hi svabhāvapratibandhe asaty ekasya nivṛttav aparasya niyamena nivṛttiḥ.
03031 sa ca dviprakāraḥ sarvasya. tādātmya-lakṣaṇas tadutpatti-lakṣaṇaś ca ity uktam.
03032 tena hi nivṛttiṃ kathayatā pratibandho darśanīyaḥ. tasmāt nivṛtti-vacanam ākṣipta-pratibandha-upadarśanam eva bhavati. yac ca pratibandha-upadarśanaṃ tad eva anvaya-vacanam ity ekena api vākyena anvaya-mukhena vyatireka-mukhena vā prayuktena sapakṣa-asapakṣayor liṅgasya sadasattva-khyāpanaṃ kṛtaṃ bhavati iti na avaśyaṃ vākya-dvaya-prayogaḥ.
03033 anupalabdhāv api: yat sad upalabdhi-lakṣaṇa-prāptaṃ tad upalabhyata eva ity ukte, anupalabhyamānaṃ tādṛśam asad iti pratīter anvaya-siddheḥ.
03034 dvayor apy anayoḥ prayogayor na avaśyaṃ pakṣa-nirdeśaḥ.
03035 yasmāt sādharmyavat-prayoge api yad upalabdhi-lakṣaṇa-prāptaṃ san na upalabhyate so asad-vyavahāra-viṣayaḥ. na upalabhyate ca atra upalabdhi-lakṣaṇa-prāpto ghaṭa ity ukte sāmarthyād eva na iha ghaṭa iti bhavati.
03036 tathā vaidharmyavat-prayoge api: yaḥ sad-vyavahāra-viṣaya upalabdhi-lakṣaṇa-prāptaḥ, sa upalabhyata eva. na tathā atra tādṛśo ghaṭa upalabhyata ity ukte sāmarthyād eva na iha sad-vyavahāra-viṣaya iti bhavati.
03037 kīdṛśaḥ punaḥ pakṣa iti nirdeśyaḥ.
03038 svarūpeṇa eva svayam iṣṭo anirākṛtaḥ pakṣa iti.
03039 svarūpeṇa iti sādhyatvena iṣṭaḥ.
03040 svarūpeṇa eva iti sādhyatvena eva iṣṭo na sādhanatvena api.
03041 yathā śabdasya anityatve sādhye cākṣuṣatvaṃ hetuḥ, śabde asiddhatvāt sādhyam. na punas tad iha sādhyatvena eva iṣṭam, sādhanatvena abhidhānāt.
03042 svayam iti vādinā.
03043 yas tadā sādhanam āha.
03044 etena yady api kvacic śāstre sthitaḥ sādhanam āha: tac śāstrakāreṇa tasmin dharmiṇy aneka-dharma-abhyupagame api yas tadā tena vādinā dharmaḥ svayaṃ sādhayitum iṣṭaḥ, sa eva sādhyo na itara ity uktaṃ bhavati.
03045 iṣṭa iti yatra arthe vivādena sādhanam upanyastaṃ tasya siddhim icchatā so anukto api vacanena sādhyaḥ.
03046 tad adhikaraṇatvād vivādasya.
03047 yathā parārthaś cakṣur-ādayaḥ saṃghātatvāc śayana-āsana-ādy-aṅga-vad iti. atra ātma-arthā ity anuktāv apy ātma-arthatā sādhyā. tena na ukta-mātram eva sādhyam ity uktaṃ bhavati.
03048 anirākṛta iti, etal-lakṣaṇa-yoge api yaḥ sādhayitum iṣṭo apy arthaḥ pratyakṣa-anumāna-pratīti-sva-vacanair nirākriyate, na sa pakṣa iti pradarśana-artham.
03049 tatra pratyakṣa-nirākṛto yathā, aśrāvaṇaḥ śabda iti.
03050 anumāna-nirākṛto yathā, nityaḥ śabda iti.
03051 pratīti-nirākṛto yathā, acandraḥ śaśī iti.
03052 sva-vacana-nirākṛto yathā, na anumānaṃ pramāṇam.
03053 iti catvāraḥ pakṣābhāsā nirākṛtā bhavanti.
03054 evaṃ siddhasya, asiddhasya api sādhanatvena abhimatasya, svayaṃ vādinā tadā sādhayitum aniṣṭasya, ukta-mātrasya ca viparyayeṇa sādhyaḥ. tena eva svarūpeṇa abhimato vādina iṣṭo anirākṛtaḥ pakṣa iti pakṣa-lakṣaṇam anavadyaṃ darśitaṃ bhavati.
03055 trirūpaliṅga-ākhyānaṃ parārtha-anumānam ity uktam. tatra trayāṇāṃ rūpāṇām ekasya api rūpasya anuktau sādhanābhāsaḥ.
03056 uktāv apy asiddhau sandehe vā pratipādya-pratipādakayoḥ.
03057 ekasya rūpasya dharmi-sambandhasya asiddhau sandehe vā asiddho hetvābhāsāḥ.
03058 yathā, anityaḥ śabda iti sādhye cākṣuṣatvam ubhaya-asiddham.
03059 cetanās tarava iti sādhye sarva-tvag-apaharaṇe maraṇaṃ prativādy-asiddham, vijñāna-indriya-āyur nirodha-lakṣaṇasya maraṇasya anena abhyupagamāt, tasya ca taruṣv asambhavāt.
03060 acetanāḥ sukha-ādaya iti sādhye utpattimatvaṃ vā sāṃkhyasya svayaṃ vādino asiddham.
03061 tathā svayaṃ tad-āśrayaṇasya vā sandehe asiddhaḥ.
03062 yathā bāṣpa-ādi-bhāvena sandihyamāno bhūta-saṃghāto agni-siddhāv upadiśyamānaḥ sandigdha-asiddhaḥ.
03063 yathā iha nikuñje mayūraḥ kekāyitād iti.
03064 tad-āpāta-deśa-vibhrame.
03065 dharmy-asiddhāv apy asiddhaḥ, yathā sarvagata ātmā iti sādhye sarvatra upalambhamāna-guṇatvam.
03066 tathā ekasya rūpasya asapakṣe asattvasya asiddhāv anaikāntiko hetvābhāsaḥ.
03067 yathā śabdasya anityatva-ādike dharme sādhye prameyatva-ādiko dharmaḥ sapakṣa-vipakṣayoḥ sarvatra ekadeśe vā vartamānaḥ.
03068 tathā, asya eva rūpasya sandehe apy anaikāntika eva.
03069 yathā asarvajñaḥ kaścid vivakṣitaḥ puruṣo rāga-ādimān vā sādhye vaktṛtva-ādiko dharmaḥ sandigdha-vipakṣa-vyāvṛttikaḥ.
03070 sarvajño vaktā na upalabhyate ity evaṃprakārasya anupalambhasya adṛśya-ātma-viṣayatvena sandeha-hetutvāt. tato asarvajña-viparyayād vaktṛtva-āder vyāvṛttiḥ sandigdhā.
03071 vaktṛtva-sarvajñatvayor virodha-abhāvāc ca yaḥ sarvajñaḥ sa vaktā na bhavati ity adarśane api vyatireko na sidhyati sandehāt.
03072 dvividho hi padārthānāṃ virodhaḥ.
03073 avikala-kāraṇasya bhavato anyabhāve abhāvād virodha-gatiḥ.
03074 śīta-uṣṇa-sparśa-vat.
03075 paraspara-parihāra-sthita-lakṣaṇatayā vā bhāva-abhāva-vat.
03076 sa ca dvividho api virodho vaktṛtva-sarvajñatvayor na sambhavati.
03077 na ca aviruddha-vidher anupalabdhāv apy abhāva-gatiḥ.
03078 rāga-ādīnāṃ vacana-ādeś ca kāryakāraṇabhāva-asiddheḥ.
03079 arthāntarasya ca akāraṇasya nivṛttau na vacana-āder nivṛttiḥ.
03080 iti sandigdha-vyatireko anaikāntiko vacana-ādiḥ.
03081 dvayo rūpayor viparyaya-siddhau viruddhaḥ.
03082 kayor dvayoḥ.
03083 sapakṣe sattvasya, asapakṣe ca asattvasya, yathā kṛtakatvaṃ prayatnānantarīyakatvaṃ ca nityatve sādhye viruddho hetvābhāsaḥ.
03084 anayoḥ sapakṣe asattvam, asapakṣe ca sattvam iti viparyaya-siddhiḥ.
03085 etau ca sādhya-viparyaya-sādhanād viruddhau.
03086 nanu ca tṛtīyo api iṣṭa-vighāta-kṛd viruddhaḥ.
03087 yathā parārthāś cakṣur-ādayaḥ saṃghātatvāc śayana-āsana-ādy-aṅga-vad iti.
03088 tad iṣṭa-saṃhata-pārārthya-viparyaya-sādhanād viruddhaḥ.
03089 sa iha kasmān na uktaḥ.
03090 anayor antarbhāvāt.
03091 na hy ayam ābhyāṃ sādhya-viparyaya-sādhanatvena bhidyate.
03092 na hi iṣṭa-uktayoḥ sādhyatvena kaścid viśeṣa iti.
03093 dvayo rūpayor ekasya asiddhāv aparasya ca sandehe anaikāntikaḥ.
03094 yathā vīta-rāgaḥ kaścit sarvajño vā, vaktṛtvād iti. vyatireko atra asiddhaḥ, sandigdho anvayaḥ.
03095 sarvajña-vīta-rāgayor viprakarṣād vacana-ādes tatra sattvam asattvaṃ vā sandigdham.
03096 anayor eva dvayo rūpayoḥ sandehe anaikāntikaḥ.
03097 yathā sātmakaṃ jīvaccharīraṃ prāṇa-ādimattvād iti.
03098 na hi sātmaka-nirātmakābhyām anyo rāśir asti yatra ayaṃ prāṇa-ādir vartate.
03099 ātmano vṛtti-vyavacchedābhyāṃ sarva-saṃgrahād.
03100 na apy anayor ekatra vṛtti-niścayaḥ.
03101 sātmakatvena anātmakatvena vā prasiddhe prāṇa-āder asiddheḥ.
03102 tasmāj jīvaccharīra-sambandhī prāṇa-ādiḥ sātmakād anātmakāc ca sarvasmād vyāvṛttatvena asiddhes tābhyāṃ na vyatiricyate.
03103 na tatra anveti.
03104 ekātmany apy asiddheḥ.
03105 na api sātmakād anātmakāc ca tasya anvaya-vyatirekayor abhāva-niścayaḥ.
03106 eka-abhāva-niścayasya apara-bhāva-niścaya-nāntarīyakatvāt.
03107 anvaya-vyatirekayor anyonya-vyavaccheda-rūpatvāt. tata eva anvaya-vyatirekayoḥ sandehād anaikāntikāḥ.
03108 sādhya-itarayor ato niścaya-abhāvāt.
03109 evam eṣāṃ trayāṇāṃ rūpāṇām ekaikasya dvayor dvayor vā rūpayor asiddhau sandehe vā yathāyogam asiddha-viruddha-anaikāntikās trayo hetvābhāsāḥ.
03110 viruddhāvyabhicāry api saṃśaya-hetur uktaḥ. sa iha kasmān na uktaḥ.
03111 anumāna-viṣaye asambhavāt.
03112 na hi sambhavo asti kārya-svabhāvayor ukta-lakṣaṇayor anupalambhasya ca viruddhatāyāḥ.
03113 na ca anyo avyabhicārī.
03114 tasmād avastu-darśana-bala-pravṛttam āgama-āśrayam anumānam āśritya tad-artha-vicāreṣu viruddhāvyabhicārī sādhana-doṣa uktaḥ.
03115 śāstrakārāṇām artheṣu bhrāntyā viparīta-svabhāva-upasaṃhāra-sambhavāt.
03116 na hy asya sambhavo yathāvasthita-vastu-sthitiṣv ātma-kārya-anupalambheṣu.
03117 tatra udāharaṇam: yat sarva-deśa-avasthitaiḥ sva-sambandhibhir yugapad abhisambadhyate tat sarvagatam, yathā ākāśam. abhisambadhyate ca sarva-deśa-avasthitaiḥ sva-sambandhibhir yugapat sāmānyam iti.
03118 tat-sambandhi-svabhāva-mātra-anubandhinī tad-deśa-saṃnihita-svabhāvatā.
03119 na hi yo yatra na asti tad-deśam ātmanā vyāpnoti iti svabhāvahetu-prayogaḥ.
03120 dvitīyo api prayogaḥ: yad upalabdhi-lakṣaṇa-prāptaṃ san na upalabhyate na tat tatra asti. tad yathā, kvacid avidyamāno ghaṭaḥ. na upalabhyate ca upalabdhi-lakṣaṇa-prāptaṃ sāmānyaṃ vyakty-antarāleṣv iti. ayam anupalambhaḥ svabhāvaś ca paraspara-viruddha-artha-sādhanād ekatra saṃśayaṃ janayataḥ.
03121 trirūpo hetur uktaḥ. tāvatā ca artha-pratītir iti na pṛthag dṛṣṭānto nāma sādhana-avayavaḥ kaścid. tena na asya lakṣaṇaṃ pṛthag ucyate gata-arthatvāt.
03122 hetoḥ sapakṣa eva sattvam asapakṣāc ca sarvato vyāvṛttī rūpam uktam abhedena. punar viśeṣeṇa kārya-svabhāvayor ukta-lakṣaṇayor janma-tan-mātra-anubandhau darśanīya-avaktau. tac ca darśayatā, yatra dhūmas tatra agniḥ, asaty agnau na kvacid dhūmo yathā mahānasa-itarayoḥ, yatra kṛtakatvaṃ tatra anityatvam, anityatva-abhāvo kṛtakatva-asambhavo yathā
ghaṭa-ākāśayoḥ, iti darśanīyam. na hy anyathā sapakṣa-vipakṣayoḥ sadasattve yathokta-prakāre śakye darśayitum. tat kāryatā-niyamaḥ kārya-liṅgasya
svabhāva-liṅgasya ca svabhāvena vyāptiḥ. asmiṃś ca arthe darśite darśita eva dṛṣṭānto bhavati. etāvān mātra-rūpatvāt tasya iti.
03123 etena eva dṛṣṭānta-doṣā api nirastā bhavanti.
03124 yathā nityaḥ śabdo amūrtatvāt. karma-vat paramāṇu-vad ghaṭa-vad iti. ete dṛṣṭāntābhāsāḥ sādhya-sādhana-dharma-ubhaya-vikalāḥ.
03125 tathā sandigdha-sādhya-dharma-ādayaś ca, yathā rāga-ādimān ayaṃ vacanād rathyā-puruṣa-vat. maraṇa-dharmo ayaṃ puruṣo rāga-ādimattvād rathyā-puruṣa-vat. asarvajño ayaṃ rāga-ādimatvād rathyā-puruṣa-vad iti.
03126 tathā ananvayo apradarśita-anvayaś ca, yathā yo uktā sa rāga-ādimān, iṣṭa-puruṣa-vat. anityaḥ śabdaḥ kṛtakatvād ghaṭa-vad iti.
03127 tathā viparīta-anvayaḥ, yad anityaṃ tat kṛtakam iti.
03128 sādharmyeṇa dṛṣṭānta-doṣāḥ.
03129 vaidharmyeṇa api, paramāṇu-vat karma-vat ākāśa-vad iti sādhya-ādy-avyatirekiṇaḥ.
03130 tathā sandigdha-sādhya-vyatireka-ādayaḥ, yathā asarvajñāḥ kapila-ādayo anāptā vā avidyamāna-sarvajñatā-āptatā-liṅgabhūta-pramāṇa-atiśaya-śāsanatvād iti. atra vaidharmya-udāharaṇam, yaḥ sarvajña āpto vā sa jyotir-jñāna-ādikam upadiṣṭavān, yathā ṛṣabha-vardhamāna-ādir iti. tatra asarvajñatā anāptayoḥ sādhya-dharmayoḥ sandigdho vyatirekaḥ.
03131 sandigdha-sādhana-vyatireko yathā, na trayīvidā brāhmaṇena grāhya-vacanaḥ kaścid vivakṣitaḥ puruṣo rāga-ādimattvād iti. atra vaidharmya-udāharaṇam, ye grāhya-vacanā na te rāga-ādimantaḥ. tad yathā gautama-ādayo dharma-śāstrāṇāṃ praṇetāra iti. gautama-ādibhyo rāga-ādimattvasya sādhana-dharmasya vyāvṛttiḥ sandigdhā.
03132 sandigdha-ubhaya-vyatireko yathā, avīta-rāgāḥ kapila-ādayaḥ, parigraha-āgraha-yogād iti. atra vaidharmyeṇa udāharaṇam, yo vīta-rāgo na tasya parigraha-āgrahaḥ, yathā ṛṣabha-āder iti. ṛṣabha-āder avīta-rāgatva-parigraha-āgraha-yogayoḥ sādhya-sādhana-dharmayoḥ sandigdho vyatirekaḥ.
03133 avyatireko yathā, avīta-rāgo ayaṃ vaktṛtvāt. vaidharmyeṇa udāharaṇam, yatra avīta-rāgatvaṃ na asti na sa vaktā, yathā upala-khaṇḍa iti. yady apy upala-khaṇḍād ubhayaṃ vyāvṛttaṃ tathā api sarvo vīta-rāgo na vaktā iti vyāptyā vyatireka-asiddher avyatirekaḥ.
03134 apradarśita-vyatireko yathā, anityaḥ śabdaḥ, kṛtakatvād ākāśa-vad iti vaidharmyeṇa.
03135 viparīta-vyatireko yathā, yad akṛtakaṃ tan nityaṃ bhavati iti.
03136 na hy ebhir dṛṣṭāntābhāsāir hetoḥ sāmānyalakṣaṇaṃ sapakṣa eva sattvaṃ vipakṣe ca sarvatra asattvam eva niścayena śakyaṃ darśayituṃ viśeṣa-lakṣaṇaṃ vā. tad arthāpattyā eṣāṃ nirāso draṣṭavyaḥ.
03137 dūṣaṇā nyūnatā-ādy-uktiḥ.
03138 ye pūrvaṃ nyūnatā-ādayaḥ sādhana-doṣā uktās teṣām udbhāvanaṃ dūṣaṇam. tena para-iṣṭa-artha-siddhi-pratibandhāt.
03139 dūṣaṇābhāsās tu jātayaḥ.
03140 abhūta-doṣa-udbhāvanāni jāty-uttarāṇi iti.

01001 The accomplishment of all human purposes is preceded by right knowledge; therefore, that [right knowledge] is explained.
01002 Right knowledge is twofold.
01003 <s>Pratyakṣa</s> (perception) and <s>anumāna</s> (inference).
01004 Therein, <s>pratyakṣa</s> (perception) is free from conceptual construction (<s>kalpanā</s>) and non-erroneous.
01005 <s>Kalpanā</s> (conceptual construction) is a cognition that appears as fit to be associated with verbal expression.
01006 A cognition that is free from that [conceptual construction] and is not subject to error caused by defective vision (<s>timira</s>), rapid movement, being on a boat, and the like, is <s>pratyakṣa</s> (perception).
01007 That is fourfold.
01008 Sense cognition (<s>indriya-jñāna</s>).
01009 Mental cognition (<s>manovijñāna</s>) is that which is produced by sense cognition—which is assisted by the object immediately following its own object—as its immediately preceding condition (<s>samanantarapratyaya</s>).
01010 Self-awareness (<s>ātma-saṃvedana</s>) of all mind (<s>citta</s>) and mental factors (<s>caitta</s>).
01011 And yogic cognition (<s>yogijñāna</s>) born from the culmination of the cultivation of a real object (<s>bhūtārtha</s>).
01012 Its object is the particular (<s>svalakṣaṇa</s>).
01013 That is a <s>svalakṣaṇa</s> (particular) whose presence and absence causes a difference in the appearance of cognition.
01014 That alone is ultimately real (<s>paramārthasat</s>).
01015 Because the nature of a real thing (<s>vastu</s>) is defined by its capacity for causal efficacy (<s>arthakriyāsāmarthya</s>).
01016 The other is the universal characteristic (<s>sāmānyalakṣaṇa</s>).
01017 That is the object of <s>anumāna</s> (inference).
01018 And that very perceptual cognition is the result of the means of valid cognition (<s>pramāṇa-phala</s>).
01019 Because it has the nature of apprehension of the object.
01020 Its conformity with the object (<s>artha-sārūpya</s>) is the means of valid cognition.
01021 Because the apprehension of the object is established by virtue of that [conformity].
02001 <s>Anumāna</s> (inference) is twofold.
02002 For oneself (<s>svārtha</s>) and for others (<s>parārtha</s>).
02003 Therein, inference for oneself (<s>svārthānumāna</s>) is the cognition of the inferable object from a logical mark (<s>liṅga</s>) possessing three characteristics.
02004 The distinction of the means of valid cognition and its result here too is like that for perception.
02005 The three characteristics (<s>trairūpya</s>) of the logical mark are: its existence only in the inferable subject, its existence only in the similar class (<s>sapakṣa</s>), and its definite non-existence in the dissimilar class (<s>asapakṣa</s>).
02006 The inferable subject (<s>anumeya</s>) here is the property-possessor (<s>dharmin</s>) with the specific property to be investigated.
02007 The similar class (<s>sapakṣa</s>) is that which shares the general property to be proved (<s>sādhya-dharma</s>).
02008 The dissimilar class (<s>asapakṣa</s>) is that which is not the similar class.
02009 It is other than that, contrary to that, and the absence of that.
02010 The logical marks possessing three characteristics are exactly three.
02011 <s>Anupalabdhi</s> (non-apprehension), <s>svabhāva</s> (essential nature), and <s>kārya</s> (effect).
02012 Therein, non-apprehension is as follows: "There is no pot in this particular location, because of the non-apprehension of what fulfills the conditions of apprehension (<s>upalabdhi-lakṣaṇa-prāpti</s>)."
02013 Fulfilling the conditions of apprehension means the completeness of the other conditions of perception and the specific nature [of the object].
02014 That specific nature is one which, when the other conditions of perception are present, would necessarily be directly perceived.
02015 <s>Svabhāva</s> (essential nature) is a reason (<s>hetu</s>) for a property to be proved that consists merely in the existence of itself.
02016 As in: "This is a tree, because of being a <s>śiṃśapā</s>."
02017 <s>Kārya</s> (effect) is as in: "There is fire here, because of smoke."
02018 Of these, two establish a positive entity; one is a reason for negation.
02019 For only when there is an essential connection (<s>svabhāvapratibandha</s>) does one thing indicate another.
02020 Because there is no invariable rule of non-deviation for what is not connected to that.
02021 And that connection of the logical mark is with the property to be proved.
02022 In reality, through identity (<s>tādātmya</s>) and through origination from that (<s>tadutpatti</s>).
02023 Because what does not have that nature and does not originate from that has an unconnected nature with regard to that.
02024 And those—identity and origination from that—belong only to essential nature and effect; therefore, establishment of a real entity is only through these two.
02025 The establishment of negation too is through non-apprehension as described.
02026 Because of the impossibility of that [non-apprehension] when the entity exists.
02027 And otherwise, because there would be no ascertainment of absence regarding objects that fulfill the conditions of apprehension but are remote in place, time, or nature, since one's own perception would not cease [even if the object were absent].
02028 The cessation of the cognizer's perception—whose memory-impressions are unconfused, regarding what is past and present—is what initiates the convention of absence.
02029 Because the ascertainment of absence is from that very [cessation of perception].
02030 And that [non-apprehension], by difference of formulation, is of eleven kinds.
02031 Non-apprehension of the essential nature (<s>svabhāva-anupalabdhi</s>), as in: "There is no smoke here, because of the non-apprehension of what fulfills the conditions of apprehension."
02032 Non-apprehension of the effect (<s>kārya-anupalabdhi</s>), as in: "The causes of smoke with unimpeded capacity are not present here, because of the absence of smoke."
02033 Non-apprehension of the pervader (<s>vyāpaka-anupalabdhi</s>), as in: "There is no <s>śiṃśapā</s> here, because of the absence of a tree."
02034 Apprehension of what is incompatible with the essential nature (<s>svabhāva-viruddha-upalabdhi</s>), as in: "There is no cold touch here, because of fire."
02035 Apprehension of the effect of what is incompatible (<s>viruddha-kārya-upalabdhi</s>), as in: "There is no cold touch here, because of smoke."
02036 Apprehension of what is pervaded by the incompatible (<s>viruddha-vyāpta-upalabdhi</s>), as in: "The destruction of an existing entity does not require the presence of smoke, because it depends on another cause."
02037 Apprehension of what is incompatible with the effect (<s>kārya-viruddha-upalabdhi</s>), as in: "The causes of cold with unimpeded capacity are not present here, because of fire."
02038 Apprehension of what is incompatible with the pervader (<s>vyāpaka-viruddha-upalabdhi</s>), as in: "There is no frost-touch here, because of fire."
02039 Non-apprehension of the cause (<s>kāraṇa-anupalabdhi</s>), as in: "There is no smoke here, because of the absence of fire."
02040 Apprehension of what is incompatible with the cause (<s>kāraṇa-viruddha-upalabdhi</s>), as in: "This [person] does not have horripilation and the like, because of being in proximity to a specific fire."
02041 Apprehension of the effect of what is incompatible with the cause (<s>kāraṇa-viruddha-kārya-upalabdhi</s>), as in: "This location does not have a person with horripilation and the like, because of smoke."
02042 All these ten non-apprehension formulations, from non-apprehension of the effect onward, are subsumed under non-apprehension of the essential nature.
02043 Even when, indirectly, the formulation differs for the purpose of establishing or negating something else.
02044 From repeated exposure to formulations, the understanding of exclusion arises by itself—therefore the exposition of formulations is given even for inference for oneself.
02045 And everywhere in this non-apprehension that establishes the convention of absence, the apprehension of the incompatible with the essential nature and the like, and the non-apprehension of causes and the like, by which negation is stated—their apprehension and non-apprehension should be understood as being of those that fulfill the conditions of apprehension.
02045 Precisely their apprehension and non-apprehension should be understood.
02046 Because the opposition and the causal relation of others [i.e., those not fulfilling the conditions] are not established.
02047 Because even when the means of valid cognition ceases, the absence of the object is not established.
03001 The declaration of the logical mark possessing three characteristics is inference for others (<s>parārthānumāna</s>).
03002 By metaphorical transference of effect to cause.
03003 That is twofold.
03004 By difference of formulation.
03005 Statement by similarity (<s>sādharmya</s>) and by dissimilarity (<s>vaidharmya</s>).
03006 There is no real difference between these two.
03007 Except for the difference in formulation.
03008 Therein, the formulation by similarity is: "Whatever fulfills the conditions of apprehension and, being existent, is not apprehended, is established as the object of the convention of non-existence, like anything else observed, such as a hare's horn. And a pot fulfilling the conditions of apprehension is not apprehended in a particular location"—this is the formulation of non-apprehension.
03009 Similarly, the formulation of the essential nature reason (<s>svabhāvahetu</s>): "Whatever exists is entirely impermanent, like a pot and the like"—this is the formulation of a pure essential nature reason.
03010 "Whatever is produced is impermanent"—this is the formulation of the essential nature through a difference of property belonging to the essential nature.
03011 "Whatever is made (<s>kṛtaka</s>) is impermanent"—through a difference of limiting condition (<s>upādhi</s>).
03012 For an entity that depends on the activity of another for the production of its nature is called <s>kṛtaka</s> (made).
03013 Thus, being differentiated by conditions and the like should also be understood similarly.
03014 "Sound is existent, or produced, or made"—this is the presentation of the property of the thesis (<s>pakṣa-dharma</s>).
03015 All these properties of the proof are [established] by their respective means of valid cognition. The property to be proved should be understood as invariably accompanying only the established property of the proof.
03016 That alone is that [i.e., the property to be proved accompanies only the established proving property].
03017 Because the essential nature is the reason.
03018 In reality, there is identity between those two.
03019 Because what is not produced when that is produced does not have the nature of that.
03020 And because deviation would be possible [otherwise].
03021 The formulation of the effect reason (<s>kāryahetu</s>): "Wherever there is smoke, there is fire, as in a kitchen and the like. And there is smoke here."
03022 Here too, when the causal relation is established and the cause is to be proved, the effect reason should be stated.
03023 The formulation by dissimilarity (<s>vaidharmya</s>): "Whatever exists and fulfills the conditions of apprehension is indeed apprehended, like blue and the like. But here the apprehension of an existing pot fulfilling the conditions of apprehension does not occur thus"—this is the formulation of non-apprehension.
03024 "In the absence of impermanence, there is absolutely no existence, or being produced, or being made. And sound is existent, or produced, or made"—this is the formulation of the essential nature reason.
03025 "In the absence of fire, there is absolutely no smoke. And there is smoke here"—this is the formulation of the effect reason.
03026 For even in a formulation by similarity, the understanding of dissimilarity follows by implication.
03027 Because in the absence of that [property to be proved], there would be no positive concomitance of the reason with the property to be proved.
03028 Similarly, even from dissimilarity, the understanding of positive concomitance follows.
03029 Because in the absence of that [property to be proved], the absence of the reason when the property to be proved is absent would not be established.
03030 For without an essential connection (<s>svabhāvapratibandha</s>), the invariable cessation of one does not follow from the cessation of another.
03031 And that [connection] is of two kinds for all. It has been said: having the nature of identity (<s>tādātmya</s>) and having the nature of origination from that (<s>tadutpatti</s>).
03032 For one who states the cessation must show the connection. Therefore, the statement of cessation is itself an indication of the implied connection. And the indication of the connection is itself the statement of positive concomitance (<s>anvaya</s>). Thus, even by a single statement, whether expressed through positive concomitance or through exclusion (<s>vyatireka</s>), the presence and absence of the logical mark in the similar and dissimilar classes is declared. Therefore, the use of two statements is not necessarily required.
03033 In non-apprehension too: when it is said "whatever exists and fulfills the conditions of apprehension is indeed apprehended," since it is understood that what is not thus apprehended and is of such a nature is non-existent, positive concomitance is established.
03034 In both of these formulations, the explicit statement of the thesis (<s>pakṣa</s>) is not necessarily required.
03035 Because even in the formulation by similarity, when it is said "whatever fulfills the conditions of apprehension and, being existent, is not apprehended, is the object of the convention of non-existence; and a pot fulfilling the conditions of apprehension is not apprehended here," by implication alone it follows that "there is no pot here."
03036 Similarly, even in the formulation by dissimilarity: when it is said "whatever is the object of the convention of existence and fulfills the conditions of apprehension is indeed apprehended; but such a pot is not apprehended here as such," by implication alone it follows that "it is not the object of the convention of existence here."
03037 What kind of thesis (<s>pakṣa</s>) should then be stated?
03038 A <s>pakṣa</s> (thesis) is what is desired by oneself in its own form and is unrefuted.
03039 "In its own form" means desired as what is to be proved (<s>sādhya</s>).
03040 "In its own form alone" means desired only as what is to be proved, not also as the means of proof (<s>sādhana</s>).
03041 For example, when impermanence of sound is to be proved and visibility (<s>cākṣuṣatva</s>) is the reason, visibility is itself unestablished in sound and hence something to be proved. But it is not desired here only as what is to be proved, since it is stated as the means of proof.
03042 "By oneself" means by the proponent (<s>vādin</s>).
03043 Who at that time states the proof.
03044 By this, even if someone established in a certain treatise states a proof, although the author of the treatise may accept many properties in that subject, only that property which the proponent himself at that time wishes to prove is what is to be proved, not another.
03045 "Desired" means: that for whose establishment a proof is presented in dispute—the one who wishes its establishment considers it to be proved even if not explicitly stated in words.
03046 Because the dispute has that as its substrate.
03047 For example: "The eyes and the like serve another's purpose, because of being an aggregate, like the limbs of a bed, seat, and the like." Here, even though "serving one's own purpose" is not explicitly stated, serving one's own purpose is what is to be negated. Thus it is indicated that not merely what is explicitly stated is what is to be proved.
03048 "Unrefuted" means: even when fitting this definition, an object that one wishes to prove but which is refuted by <s>pratyakṣa</s> (perception), <s>anumāna</s> (inference), common understanding (<s>pratīti</s>), or one's own words (<s>sva-vacana</s>), is not a valid thesis—this is shown for the purpose of demonstration.
03049 Therein, refuted by perception, as in: "Sound is inaudible."
03050 Refuted by inference, as in: "Sound is permanent."
03051 Refuted by common understanding, as in: "The moon is not 'the moon' [<s>śaśin</s>]."
03052 Refuted by one's own words, as in: "Inference is not a means of valid cognition."
03053 Thus four pseudo-theses (<s>pakṣābhāsa</s>) are refuted.
03054 Thus, by reversal of what is [already] established, of what is accepted as the means of proof though unestablished, of what the proponent himself does not wish to prove at that time, and of what is merely stated—[one arrives at] what is to be proved. Therefore, it is shown that the definition of the thesis—"desired by the proponent himself in its own form and unrefuted"—is faultless.
03055 It has been said that the declaration of the logical mark possessing three characteristics is inference for others. Therein, when even one of the three characteristics is not stated, it is a pseudo-proof (<s>sādhanābhāsa</s>).
03056 Even when stated, if unestablished or doubtful for either what is to be communicated or the means of communication.
03057 When one characteristic—the connection with the subject (<s>dharmin</s>)—is unestablished or doubtful, the reason is unestablished (<s>asiddha</s>)—these are pseudo-reasons (<s>hetvābhāsa</s>).
03058 For example, when impermanence of sound is to be proved, visibility (<s>cākṣuṣatva</s>) is unestablished for both parties.
03059 When sentience of trees is to be proved, death upon complete removal of bark is unestablished for the opponent, because he accepts death as the cessation of consciousness, senses, and life-force, and that is impossible in trees.
03060 When non-sentience of pleasure and the like is to be proved, being produced (<s>utpattimatva</s>) is unestablished for the <s>Sāṃkhya</s> proponent himself.
03061 Similarly, when there is doubt about the [reason] itself or its basis, it is unestablished.
03062 For example, a collection of elements whose nature as vapor and the like is doubtful, when presented to establish fire, is doubtfully unestablished.
03063 As in: "There is a peacock in this thicket, because of the cry."
03064 When there is confusion about the location from which the sound comes.
03065 When the subject (<s>dharmin</s>) is unestablished, [the reason is] also unestablished, as in when the omnipresence of the self (<s>ātman</s>) is to be proved, the reason being "having qualities that are perceived everywhere."
03066 Similarly, when one characteristic—the non-existence in the dissimilar class—is unestablished, the pseudo-reason is inconclusive (<s>anaikāntika</s>).
03067 For example, when impermanence and the like are to be proved of sound, the property of being knowable (<s>prameyatva</s>) and the like, which exists everywhere or in part in both the similar and dissimilar classes.
03068 Similarly, when this very characteristic is doubtful, it is also inconclusive.
03069 For example, when it is to be proved that a specific intended person is not omniscient or has passions, the property of being a speaker (<s>vaktṛtva</s>) and the like has doubtful exclusion from the dissimilar class.
03070 Because the non-apprehension of the type "no omniscient speaker is observed" is a cause of doubt, since it concerns an invisible self. Therefore, the exclusion of being a speaker and the like from the opposite of non-omniscience is doubtful.
03071 And because there is no incompatibility between being a speaker and being omniscient, even when it is not observed that "whoever is omniscient is not a speaker," the exclusion is not established, due to doubt.
03072 For the incompatibility of entities is twofold.
03073 The understanding of incompatibility arises because when all causes are complete, an entity ceases to exist in the presence of another.
03074 Like cold and hot touches.
03075 Or by having mutually exclusive defining characteristics, like existence and non-existence.
03076 And neither kind of incompatibility is possible between being a speaker and being omniscient.
03077 And when what is not incompatible is not apprehended, absence is not understood.
03078 Because the causal relation between passions and speech and the like is not established.
03079 And when something that is not a cause—something different—ceases, speech and the like do not cease.
03080 Thus, speech and the like, with doubtful exclusion, are inconclusive (<s>anaikāntika</s>).
03081 When the opposite of two characteristics is established, [the reason is] contradictory (<s>viruddha</s>).
03082 Which two?
03083 Of existence in the similar class and non-existence in the dissimilar class—for example, being made (<s>kṛtakatva</s>) and being immediately preceded by effort (<s>prayatnānantarīyakatva</s>), when permanence is to be proved, are contradictory pseudo-reasons.
03084 The opposite of these is established: non-existence in the similar class and existence in the dissimilar class.
03085 And these two are contradictory because they prove the opposite of what is to be proved.
03086 But is there not a third kind of contradictory reason that obstructs what is desired?
03087 For example: "The eyes and the like serve another's purpose, because of being an aggregate, like the limbs of a bed, seat, and the like."
03088 That is contradictory because it proves the opposite of the desired [conclusion that] aggregated things serve another's purpose.
03089 Why is it not mentioned here?
03090 Because it is included in those two.
03091 For this does not differ from those two in being a proof of the opposite of what is to be proved.
03092 For there is no difference between what is desired and what is stated as what is to be proved.
03093 When one of the two characteristics is unestablished and the other is doubtful, [the reason is] inconclusive.
03094 For example: "Someone is free from passion or omniscient, because of being a speaker." The exclusion (<s>vyatireka</s>) here is unestablished, and the positive concomitance (<s>anvaya</s>) is doubtful.
03095 Because omniscience and freedom from passion are remote [from being a speaker], the presence or absence of speech and the like therein is doubtful.
03096 When these very two characteristics are both doubtful, [the reason is] inconclusive.
03097 For example: "A living body has a self (<s>ātman</s>), because of having breath (<s>prāṇa</s>) and the like."
03098 For there is no other class besides those with a self and those without a self in which this breath and the like exists.
03099 Because of the complete inclusion [of all things] through the presence and absence of the self.
03100 Nor is there certainty of its existence in either one.
03101 Because breath and the like, as known to possess a self or to be without a self, is unestablished.
03102 Therefore, breath and the like connected with a living body, being unestablished as excluded from everything with and without a self, is not excluded from those two.
03103 Nor does it positively accompany them.
03104 Because it is unestablished even in one [of them].
03105 Nor is there certainty of the absence of its positive and negative concomitance with what has a self and what lacks a self.
03106 Because the certainty of absence in one necessarily entails the certainty of presence in the other.
03107 Because positive and negative concomitance have the form of mutual exclusion. Therefore, from the doubt in both positive and negative concomitance, [the reasons are] inconclusive.
03108 Because there is no certainty regarding what is to be proved or the alternative.
03109 Thus, when one or two of these three characteristics are unestablished or doubtful, the three pseudo-reasons (<s>hetvābhāsa</s>)—unestablished (<s>asiddha</s>), contradictory (<s>viruddha</s>), and inconclusive (<s>anaikāntika</s>)—arise as appropriate.
03110 The contradictory-non-deviating (<s>viruddhāvyabhicārin</s>) has also been called a cause of doubt. Why is it not mentioned here?
03111 Because it is impossible in the domain of [proper] inference.
03112 For there is no possibility of contradiction between effect (<s>kārya</s>) and essential nature (<s>svabhāva</s>) as defined, or of non-apprehension (<s>anupalabdhi</s>).
03113 And there is no other non-deviating [reason].
03114 Therefore, relying on inference based on scripture—which proceeds from the force of perceiving what is unreal—the contradictory-non-deviating was stated as a defect of proof in the examination of the meaning of scripture.
03115 Because it is possible for authors of treatises to erroneously subsume things of opposite nature.
03116 For it is not possible regarding the actual state of things, with [reasons that are] essential nature, effect, and non-apprehension.
03117 An example therein: "Whatever is simultaneously connected with its own relata located in all places is omnipresent, like <s>ākāśa</s> (space). And a universal (<s>sāmānya</s>) is simultaneously connected with its own relata located in all places."
03118 Being located in a certain place is invariably accompanied by having a nature that accompanies merely the nature of what is related to it.
03119 For what does not exist somewhere does not pervade that place by itself—this is the formulation of the essential nature reason.
03120 The second formulation: "Whatever fulfills the conditions of apprehension and, being existent, is not apprehended, does not exist there—like a pot that does not exist somewhere. And a universal (<s>sāmānya</s>) fulfilling the conditions of apprehension is not apprehended in the intervals between individuals." This non-apprehension and the essential nature [reason], proving mutually contradictory objects, generate doubt regarding a single [subject].
03121 A reason possessing three characteristics has been stated. And since the apprehension of the object is accomplished by that much, there is no separate component of proof called "example" (<s>dṛṣṭānta</s>). Therefore, its definition is not separately stated, since its purpose has been served.
03122 The characteristic of the reason—its existence only in the similar class and its exclusion from all of the dissimilar class—has been stated without distinction. Further, specifically for effect and essential nature as defined, the invariable accompaniment with origination and mere nature respectively must be shown but has not been stated. And one showing this must demonstrate: "Wherever there is smoke, there is fire; where there is no fire, there is nowhere smoke, as in a kitchen and elsewhere; wherever there is being-made, there is impermanence; where impermanence is absent, being-made is impossible, as in a pot and space." For otherwise, the presence and absence in the similar and dissimilar classes in the manner described cannot be shown. That is the invariable relation (<s>niyama</s>) of the effect-mark and the pervasion (<s>vyāpti</s>) of the essential-nature-mark by the essential nature. And when this meaning is shown, the example is shown, because the example consists of just this much.
03123 By this, the defects of examples are also eliminated.
03124 For example: "Sound is permanent, because of being incorporeal—like action, like an atom, like a pot." These are pseudo-examples (<s>dṛṣṭāntābhāsa</s>) lacking the property to be proved, the proving property, or both.
03125 Similarly, those with doubtful property to be proved and the like: "This person has passions, because of speaking, like a person on the street. This person is subject to death, because of having passions, like a person on the street. This person is not omniscient, because of having passions, like a person on the street."
03126 Similarly, those without positive concomitance (<s>anvaya</s>) or with undemonstrated positive concomitance: "Whoever speaks has passions, like a desired person. Sound is impermanent, because of being made, like a pot."
03127 Similarly, with reversed positive concomitance: "Whatever is impermanent is made."
03128 These are defects of examples by similarity.
03129 By dissimilarity too: "like an atom, like action, like space"—those that do not exclude the property to be proved and the like.
03130 Similarly, those with doubtful exclusion of the property to be proved and the like: "<s>Kapila</s> and others are not omniscient, or are not authoritative, because of teaching scriptures that lack the excellence of the means of valid cognition which is the mark of omniscience or authoritativeness." Here the dissimilarity example is: "Whoever is omniscient or authoritative has taught astronomy and the like, like <s>Ṛṣabha</s>, <s>Vardhamāna</s>, and others." Therein, the exclusion of the properties to be proved—non-omniscience and non-authoritativeness—is doubtful.
03131 Doubtful exclusion of the proving property: "A certain intended person should not be accepted by a <s>brāhmaṇa</s> versed in the three <s>Vedas</s>, because of having passions." Here the dissimilarity example is: "Those whose words should be accepted do not have passions, like <s>Gautama</s> and other authors of <s>Dharmaśāstras</s>." The exclusion of the proving property—having passions—from <s>Gautama</s> and others is doubtful.
03132 Doubtful exclusion of both: "<s>Kapila</s> and others have not abandoned passions, because of attachment to possessions." Here the dissimilarity example is: "One who has abandoned passions has no attachment to possessions, like <s>Ṛṣabha</s> and others." The exclusion from <s>Ṛṣabha</s> and others of both the properties to be proved and proving—not having abandoned passions and attachment to possessions—is doubtful.
03133 Non-exclusion (<s>avyatireka</s>): "This person has not abandoned passions, because of being a speaker. The dissimilarity example: where there is no non-abandonment of passions, there is no speaking, like a stone slab." Although both are excluded from the stone slab, since the full pervasion "every one who has abandoned passions is not a speaker" is not established, it is non-exclusion.
03134 Undemonstrated exclusion: "Sound is impermanent, because of being made, like space"—by dissimilarity.
03135 Reversed exclusion: "Whatever is not made is permanent."
03136 For by these pseudo-examples, neither the general characteristic—the reason's existence only in the similar class and its complete non-existence in the dissimilar class—nor the specific characteristic can be shown with certainty. Therefore, their elimination should be seen as following by implication.
03137 Refutation (<s>dūṣaṇa</s>) is the statement of incompleteness (<s>nyūnatā</s>) and other [defects].
03138 The bringing to light of those defects of proof—incompleteness and the like—stated earlier is refutation. Because it obstructs the establishment of what is desired by the opponent.
03139 Pseudo-refutations (<s>dūṣaṇābhāsa</s>) are futile rejoinders (<s>jāti</s>).
03140 Replies pointing out non-existent defects are futile rejoinders (<s>jāti</s>).
